title: Multi-source/LLM sentiment substituted into the SAME weight-preset formulas that rejected the old signal

tables.name: Richer-signal weight substitutions vs baseline vs random control

notes: performance.json only keeps a rolling ~14-day window, so this only covers 2026-07-30 onward -- smaller sample than stone 1's already-thin dataset. Substitutes multi_source_sentiment.py's pooled score and llm_news_sentiment.py's Opus-graded score into backtest.py's EXACT already-tested balanced/accum55 weight formulas, isolating whether the blend structure itself is the problem (as opposed to the old thin signal specifically). Stone #2 of 6 in the user's 2026-08-18 'turn over every stone' sentiment review.

conclusion.summary: 0/4 richer-signal weight substitutions beat both the real baseline and their own random-shuffle control. The blend structure itself appears to be the limiting factor, not just the old signal quality -- consistent with stone 1s finding that the mechanical top-3 is already hard to beat by reranking on any sentiment source.
